Codex review: needs maintainer review before merge. ## What this changes This PR bundles Knowledge as an optional memory plugin with evidence-backed records, retrieval, shared stores, and a Control UI explorer. **Example:** An operator selects plugins.slots.memory: "knowledge". - **Before:** Knowledge requires a separately installed plugin. - **After:** The bundled plugin provides Knowledge tools and its explorer without a separate installation. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | Useful and supported by shipped-entry-point evidence, with no introduced blocking defect identified; exact-head core CI attribution remains unresolved. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦞 diamond lobster **(5/6)** | Sufficient (live_output): Bundled-Gateway output exercises real-model memory writes, private-versus-conversation isolation, operator denials, and workspace attachment success and escape rejection; the later production-owner harness records reset, reassignment, and operator-revocation rejection before final effects, with the relevant Knowledge paths unchanged. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Product **Kind:** Feature · **Worth it:** Yes · **Fix scope:** Complete **User problem:** Users must separately install Knowledge, and its independent distribution can drift from OpenClaw. **Reason:** Maintainer-authored direction makes this an approved optional integration, with existing memory selection and other providers preserved. ## Merge readiness ✅ **Ready for maintainer review** Keep this maintainer-authored PR open: optional Knowledge bundling has clear value, and the previously reported physical-store pinning defect is fixed. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `9f4f07a64002fbe871b95a52d975ad022d666295` ## Before merge None. ## Findings None.
Agent review details ### How this fits together Knowledge consumes host-issued agent and operator authority, resolves the authorized store and partition, and serves memory operations through plugin-owned workers and vault files. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Agent tools] --> C[Knowledge service] B[Control UI] --> C C --> D[Host authority and store resolution] D --> E[Storage worker] E --> F[SQLite journal and search index] E --> G[Markdown vault and evidence] ``` ### Technical review Best possible solution: Bundle Knowledge through the existing plugin owners while preserving live authority checks, existing stores, and the documented standalone transition. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? This is a feature import; source inspection confirms that Knowledge is absent from fetched main and registered by this PR. Is this the best way to solve the issue? The implementation fits the existing feature-plugin, memory-provider, worker, and config-writer owners without introducing a competing core memory system. AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. Codex review notes: model internal, reasoning medium; reviewed against [ec3cfa5f72da](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ec3cfa5f72daba38d22a7b0a257e092112ae014c). ### Provenance checked - `Generic plugin session actions` keeps the original intent (1adaa28dc86b4eb5805733f558962481159678f3: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/72287 established generic host hooks so workflow plugins could integrate without product-specific core patches.) - `Session-action reload and live policy` keeps the original intent (4bbb8154288d9ebeb2d84faa946948820914dcf5: The existing handler retries actions across plugin reload; this PR retains that dispatch and adds the request-authority callback needed at configuration publication.) - `Learning command descriptions` keeps the original intent (f8d9d253e1c4bf4433d32f9827d5f078fa377112: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181879 already added memory-backed learning; this PR aligns command descriptions and supplies the participating plugin.) - `SQLite dialect inventory` changes intended behavior with a stated reason (a1c1610b1907a3750f623297af19dedd425f7399: The shrink-only inventory exposes SQLite-specific debt; the maintainer explains the narrow exception for Knowledge's rebuildable plugin-private FTS index and adds scope controls.) ### Testing Proof path: shipped entry point. ### Security None. ### Evidence What I checked: - **Optional plugin integration:** The entry composes existing feature-plugin and plugin-entry contracts; the manifest declares the memory kind, tools, skills, and packaged UI. The fetched main tree has no extensions/knowledge entry. ([`extensions/knowledge/src/index.ts:8`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9f4f07a64002fbe871b95a52d975ad022d666295/extensions/knowledge/src/index.ts#L8), [9f4f07a64002](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/9f4f07a64002fbe871b95a52d975ad022d666295)) - **Previous index finding resolved:** The pinned-index identity includes runtime.vaultId alongside agent, session incarnation, binding, and cutoff; the regression test exercises a binding moving between physical stores. **Subject inference (`subject-infer.ts`): keeping as-is.**

When the agent passes `subject`, `knowledge_remember` resolves it by exact page ID, title or alias and never guesses. Inference runs only when `subject` is omitted and `infer_subject` is not `false`. It links a claim only when the claim text names exactly one current entity page by exact ID, title or alias, and names no other capitalized name. Bare first names that only prefix a title, two resolved entities, or any competing name leave the claim unlinked.

In the example, "Atlas acquired nimbus." links to Atlas, which is the claim's subject. A claim only ever links to a page its text names, and keyword search still finds the claim through "nimbus".

Removing inference means claims saved without `subject` never appear on entity pages, and the maintenance relink pass links only claims that carry a `source_page`. That would cut what every entity page shows in order to change how a lowercase second name is handled. Claims the deterministic pass leaves unlinked go to the agent through the `knowledge-unlinked-claims` skill, which chooses their subject pages with judgment. This is exact-match identity resolution with deterministic rules, not interpretation of meaning, and I couldn't find the contract cited in the finding in the repository's `AGENTS.md` files or review docs.

**Revocation across pending publication: what is proven, and why there is no production trace of a queued race.**

The PR body now includes a bundled-Gateway trace for `knowledge_attach_file`: an authorized 87-byte transfer completes with matching SHA-256, and `../`, symlink and absolute-path escapes are refused, with nothing from outside the workspace retained.

For the two queued-effect traces, the guards sit at the point of effect, and deterministic tests cover them:

- **Record and attachment publication after reset or reassignment.** The storage worker holds no authority. Every `access.assertCurrent()` in storage, including the checks immediately before each publication step and before each attachment chunk is installed, blocks the worker until the main thread re-resolves the caller's live audience (`StorageClient.receive`, `storage-client.ts:118`). Work that waits in the queue while a session resets or a store is reassigned fails its next check before any file is installed. Tests: `publication.test.ts > authority expires after acceptance: no new files; original scope can resume` revokes between acceptance and publication; `stores.test.ts > the cutover fences old-assignment access before applying and after` covers reassignment.
- **Membership persistence after operator revocation.** `plugins.sessionAction` gives handlers a live `client.assertCurrent()` backed by the Gateway's request authority, and `store-assignments.ts` passes it to the config writer as `writeOptions.assertCurrent`, which the writer checks at publication, the same mechanism `config.patch` uses. Tests: `stores.test.ts > an operator whose access ends before the config write changes nothing`; `plugin-host-hooks.registry.test.ts` asserts that `assertCurrent` throws once the connection's grant is revoked.

A production trace of either race needs work held between acceptance and publication. The shipped build has no pause point there, and adding a test-only seam to production code is against repository rules. A timing-based trace would be nondeterministic and would prove less than the tests above. I'm treating these two traces as not required and leaving that call to maintainer review.

nodes.body:
## Final-effect proof: pending Knowledge writes after authority revocation

This addresses the review request for proof that pending Knowledge writes have no final effect once their authority is revoked. It also shows store reassignment going through the **real** config writer, not a substitute.

**Result: 5/5 scenarios passed on a Crabbox/Blacksmith testbox at this PR's head.**

- Source: `8abb780f832897b8f563cea14fd19330e159c9ac` (tree `2c6d32f99b6a`; Crabbox verified the source, carrier `c0ab1772add4`)
- Run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40158613826 (`runStatus=succeeded`, `exitCode=0`, Node v24.22.1)
- No production code was modified. The disposable harness runs the PR source through `scripts/tsx.mjs`, and the run checks that the checkout is clean.

### Method

A driver attaches the Node inspector to a target process, including its Knowledge worker threads. The target registers the real Knowledge plugin entry and calls the registered tools and operator session actions. For each scenario:

1. Save a control page and a control attachment, both successfully.
2. Start a pending `knowledge_save_page` or `knowledge_attach`, and pause it in the worker at its last authority check before the final effect:
   - `storage-journal.ts`: `access.assertCurrent()` before `files.publish(change, …)`
   - `attachments.ts`: the `current()` check before `fs.linkSync(staging, …)`
3. While it is paused, revoke authority through the production owner.
4. Resume, then check the tool outcome, the files on disk and the persisted config bytes.

| Scenario | Revocation owner | Pending write outcome | Files from the pending write | Config |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| record-reset | `performGatewaySessionReset` (real session store and turn admission) | `admitted run authority is no longer active` | none | unchanged |
| attachment-reset | same | `admitted run authority is no longer active` | none | unchanged |
| record-reassign | `stores_change` share_existing → `Stores.cutover` → real `mutateConfigFile` | `This agent's knowledge store assignment changed; retry the original request.` | none | reassignment `applied` by the real writer |
| attachment-reassign | same | same | none (no promoted artifact) | reassignment `applied` by the real writer |
| membership-revoke | `invalidateGatewayDeviceRevocation` while `stores_change` is paused inside the real config writer (`backup-rotation.ts` `replaceFileAtomicSync`) | real writer refuses: `Config write failed after source ownership changed: Gateway requester authority changed`; change reports `not-applied` | — | bytes identical (sha256 matched before and after) |

For the reassign scenarios, the driver also paused `Stores.cutover` at the lane drain and evaluated `this.fenced.has("main") === true`. This confirms the cutover fences the agent before the in-flight write resumes. It also showed that the operator `stores_snapshot` call waits behind an in-flight publication. The harness therefore takes the snapshot before starting the pending write.

The reset scenarios check that the old invocation's `assertInvocationCurrent()` fails after the reset commits. They do not assume the reset rotates the session ID.

The same harness also passed 5/5 locally on the same head before the testbox run.
